messages:
sarah_customer: Hey support — we rotated our service key this morning and now every request to /v1/chat returns 401 invalid_api_key. Worked before rotation. Any ideas?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting that. Can you paste the curl you used (redact the middle of the key) and the full raw response from the API (including headers)? Also want the request id if present.

sarah_customer: here's what I ran (redacted):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123XYZ
' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized and body: `\{"error\":\{"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"Invalid API key\"\}\}`
Request-ID: req_7f9c2b4a

alex_support: ok that curl has a suspicious trailing newline inside the single quotes after the key — looks like the header value includes a CR/LF which the server treats as malformed token. Can you try without the trailing newline: `-H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123XYZ'` (no extra \n inside the quotes) or use double quotes on mac/linux shells: `-H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\"`.

alex_support: also quick check — did you create a 'client-side' key by mistake? Some keys are restricted (public/embed keys) and will return 401 for server endpoints. Where did you create it (Console > API Keys)?

sarah_customer: created through Console > API keys > Create service key. I copied from the modal. I usually copy/paste into a local config and then export it. Noticed my editor appended a newline when I pasted.

alex_support: yep that matches. Two things to try: 1) rotate the key again and copy with `echo -n $KEY` to avoid trailing newline, 2) run this repro (sanitized):
```
KEY=\"sk_live_...\"
printf \"%s\" \"$KEY\" | xxd -p
# should show hex with no 0a at end
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-redwood-1\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hello\"}]}'
```

alex_support: If you still see 401 after removing trailing newline, paste the `curl -v` request/response. Also include the Request-ID header value.

ci-bot: log: api-auth-service accepted token check failed for request req_7f9c2b4a -> reason: invalid-token-format (CRLF in header)

jamie_sre: jumped in and followed logs for req_7f9c2b4a — server shows token value ends with 0x0a (LF). It fails our token regex validation and returns 401 invalid_api_key. Not an auth backend issue — it's header formatting. I grep'd for recent rotations from the customer's org and see two keys created at 2026-11-03T10:13:02Z and 10:15:01Z; the first was copied into a .env with trailing newline.

jamie_sre: Quick mitigation for customer: rotate the key from console (create new service key), then use the following to validate before using: `printf \"%s\" \"sk_live_NEWKEY\" | wc -c` — should match expected length (no extra chars). After that `curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_NEWKEY\\\" ...` should succeed.

alex_support: I've opened ticket SUP-54321 and added SRE notes and logs. Marking as customer-action: rotate and confirm. If they can't rotate due to automation, we can temporarily whitelist the exact token string for 30 minutes while they fix, but we'd prefer rotation.

sarah_customer: rotated and tested with `printf` check — it works now. No more 401. Thanks!

alex_support: great — closing the loop. For future: avoid editors that append newline to copied secrets; use `printf`/`echo -n` to verify; and if you ever see a 401, include the Request-ID and a `curl -v` dump so we can check server-side validation. :thumbsup:
